text: Hello everyone! In this video, I'll walk you through Analytivest. Invest with evidence. It's a data-led analysis app for Indian stocks and IPOs on NSE and BSE. First, the problems we all face. Then, how Analytivest solves them.

Problem one: tips and hype. WhatsApp forwards, Telegram calls, grey market premium and subscription headlines push us into decisions without evidence. Problem two: data is scattered across annual reports, exchange filings, websites, and five-hundred-page RHPs. Problem three: most apps give one buy or sell rating, with no reasons, and lots of jargon. And problem four: hidden traps. Bonus issues distort EPS, some companies report in dollars, one-time gains inflate profits, and sometimes the data itself is wrong.

Analytivest gives you three separate verdicts. Business quality: is the company strong? Financial risk: how vulnerable is it? And valuation: is the price reasonable? Every number shows its source, period and formula.
Just type a company name or NSE symbol. If the same company is listed on NSE and BSE, it groups them together, with NSE as the default.

Here is TCS. On top, the summary: strong fundamentals, with confidence and data completeness. Click why this score, to see what drove it. The fair-value range shows where today's price sits. Below, price and profit trends, plus positive factors and major risks, each backed by evidence.
Every tab goes deeper. Financials, growth, debt and cash flow. Each chart has period selectors and a table view, and every jargon term has a simple explanation on hover.

In valuation, you get multiples with their basis, the historical P/E band, and a DCF you can edit live. Change the growth rate, and the value and sensitivity grid update instantly. Peer comparison even catches bad provider data, and keeps it out of the averages.

The risks tab is an automated red-flag system. For this sample company, it catches negative free cash flow, weak cash conversion, exceptional gains and dilution, each with evidence, severity and period. Signals to check, not accusations.

And those hidden traps? HDFC Bank gets a bank-specific model, with its bonus issue adjusted. Infosys's dollar figures are converted to rupees. And demerger gains are excluded, so profit reflects the continuing business.

Now, the IPO module. Upload the RHP or DRHP in any format: PDF, Word, even scanned images. Analytivest extracts the price band, fresh issue versus offer for sale, financials, peers and risks, and shows the exact page for every number. Then you get a clear suggestion: apply, borderline or skip, with reasons. Grey market premium and subscription numbers are ignored on purpose.
You also get side-by-side comparison of up to five companies, a watchlist, saved snapshots, CSV and PDF export, dark mode, and a mobile-friendly layout.
Remember, Analytivest is decision support, not investment advice. So that's Analytivest. Invest with evidence. Thanks for watching, and happy investing!
